checks.invariant: Attacker-chosen instruction-file names/paths/content reach the web/CLI/download sinks only through autoescape+_shown/_oneline (web) or _safe (CLI): no markup/attribute injection, no bidi/invisible reordering, no fake rows/lines, and no Content-Disposition header injection.
checks.result:
Rendering _outbox.html/_created.html with a name containing quotes, , raw newline, U+202E and U+0001: markup is HTML-escaped, href is percent-encoded via |urlencode, the download attribute is escaped, and _created.html's |oneline escapes the newline so no fake
  • row appears. _shown escapes Cf/Cc everywhere; only \n survives raw, which cannot break out of a quoted attribute or create a new row. api.outbox_file uses urllib.parse.quote(name), so CR/LF become %0D/%0A and there is no header injection. sandbox.html upload JS writes via textContent. CLI _safe/_show_approval escape every attacker field and split content per line. No injection observed.

checks.invariant: Rendering up to 20 pending full-content instruction-file approval cards per sandbox (1 MiB each), re-polled every 2 s, must not cost the control plane seconds of CPU or tens of MiB per poll.
checks.result: write_file content is exempt from TOOL_ARG_MAX (service.py:359), bounded only by max_write_bytes=1 MiB (config.py:59); PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 per sandbox (service.py:47). _approvals.html:13 renders a.args.content in full through _shown (control characters expand about 4x). Measured with the real web filters: 20 cards x 1 MiB of U+0001 content rendered in 10.110 s and produced an 80.0 MiB (83,909,242 byte) response. index.html:25 polls /ui/approvals (all sandboxes) every 2 s, and web.render (web.py:148) builds and SHA-256-hashes the whole body even to return a 204.

checks.invariant: with_notice wraps instruction-file content in a per-call unforgeable random-tag boundary that content cannot imitate; the truncation marker sits inside the boundary; MCP and the built-in loop produce the same enclosure.
checks.result: with_notice draws tag=secrets.token_hex(8) and redraws while tag in text (instruction_files.py:132-134). Content containing the full NOTICE text plus a fake boundary with tag 'deadbeef' stayed strictly inside the real random-tag boundary, and the notice states a boundary line lacking the real tag is file text. The truncation marker is added before wrapping, so it is inside the boundary. Divergence: when the wrapped text exceeds agent.py _RESULT_LIMIT=20000, ToolClient.call_text truncates text[:20000]+marker (agent.py:126-127) and drops the closing boundary line, while mcp_server.read_file keeps it. No boundary failure results because the attacker cannot emit the random tag, so this is hardening.

checks.invariant: exec results carry a notice only (no boundary, by design); read classification uses the requested path; list_dir carries neither; reads through a link or non-instruction name are governed by the documented name-only limitation.
checks.result: service._run_tool sets res['notice'] for exec when paths_in_words hits (service.py:138-141) with no boundary, and call_text/MCP return exec/list_dir without with_notice, matching the design. read_file goes through IF.mark_read on the requested path with no link resolution, so reading an instruction file through a link (notes.md -> CLAUDE.md) yields no notice and would bypass a user read rule; this is the documented name-only limitation and is recorded as hardening (write side resolves links, read side does not).

candidates.title: Instruction-file approval cards render attacker-sized full content with no per-card or aggregate cap, polled every 2 s
candidates.description: A prompt-injected sandbox agent can queue up to PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 pending instruction-file write approvals per sandbox, each carrying up to max_write_bytes=1 MiB of agent-chosen content (write_file 'content' is exempt from TOOL_ARG_MAX). The approval UI renders every pending card's content in full through autoescape + _shown (escape_controls), with no truncation and no aggregate cap, and the index approvals fragment aggregates the pending set of every sandbox. Measured locally with the real web filters: 20 cards x 1 MiB of control-byte content rendered in 10.11 s and produced an 80 MiB response body. index.html:25 re-polls /ui/approvals every 2 s and web.render builds and SHA-256-hashes the full body even to return a 204, so the cost is paid on every poll and multiplied by the number of sandboxes. The human approval view becomes unusable and control-plane threadpool workers are tied up while the human is trying to triage the attacker's pending writes.
candidates.root_cause: _approvals.html:13 renders a.args.content in full with no length bound; escape_controls expands each control character about 4x; there is no per-card content cap and no aggregate rendered-bytes cap on the approvals fragment; web.render always materialises and hashes the whole body even when it will return 204; write_file content bypasses TOOL_ARG_MAX so one card can be 1 MiB, with 20 pending per sandbox, and the index fragment aggregates all sandboxes.
candidates.intended_behavior: The approvals view, polled every 2 s on the index and sandbox pages, must bound the CPU and bytes a single poll costs so that attacker-chosen pending content cannot make each poll cost seconds of control-plane CPU or tens of MiB of response.

trace.description: The TOOL_ARG_MAX check excludes the 'content' key, so write_file content is bounded only by max_write_bytes (1 MiB).
approvals.create stores the full args (including 1 MiB content); up to PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 rows can be pending per sandbox.
Lists every pending approval; with sandbox_id=None (the index poll) it aggregates all sandboxes into one fragment.
Builds the entire response body and hashes it on every request, even when it returns 204.

evidence.description: max_write_bytes = 1024 * 1024, the only bound on write_file content size.
Local measurement: 20 x 1 MiB control-byte cards render in 10.110 s producing an 80.0 MiB body using the real web filters and _approvals.html.

conditions.description: Attacker holds a per-sandbox agent token (the assumed prompt-injected agent).
A human has an approvals view open; the index and sandbox pages poll /ui/approvals every 2 s automatically.
Up to 20 pending instruction-file write approvals per sandbox, each about 1 MiB of control-byte content.

execution.attacker_perspective: As the sandbox agent, fill the per-sandbox pending queue with maximum-size instruction-file writes; every human poll of the approvals view then re-renders them.
payloads: repeat 20 times with different instruction-file paths to reach PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX
instructions: In the sandbox, build a Jinja2 environment for agentbox/templates with autoescape on, finalize=agentbox.web._shown, and filters oneline/short as in web.register.
Construct 20 pending-approval dicts with tool='write_file', preview.instruction_file set, and args.content = '\x01' * (1024*1024).
Render _approvals.html once and record render time and body size.
execution.observed_result: Rendering 20 pending cards x 1 MiB control-byte content took 10.110 s and produced an 80.0 MiB (83,909,242 byte) body.

remediation.strategy: Show only a capped prefix of instruction-file content in the 2 s-polled list, with a separate non-polled 'view full content' page for the approval being inspected; cap aggregate rendered bytes per fragment; avoid rebuilding and rehashing an unchanged large fragment on every poll.

likelihood.reason: Triggered by a prompt-injected agent under default configuration; the UI polls automatically.

impact.reason: Degrades or denies the human approval UI and ties up control-plane threadpool workers while the human triages the attacker's writes; no data loss or privilege change.

confidence.reason: Measured locally with the real web filters and template; bounds and per-poll rebuild are source-confirmed.

hardening: agent.py ToolClient.call_text truncates the already-wrapped read result at _RESULT_LIMIT=20000 (agent.py:126-127), dropping the closing boundary line for large instruction files, while mcp_server.read_file keeps it; apply the length limit before with_notice wraps it.

Read classification does not resolve links (service._resolved only resolves write_file/delete_file), so reading an instruction file through a link yields no notice and could bypass a user read-block rule; resolving the read target as writes do would close the asymmetry.
escape_controls expands each control character to a 4-6 char escape; sinks that render attacker-sized strings through _shown should cap input length before escaping.
